## 60a64cbfe154

**Reproduced in-domain shortcut gap.** Generator SHA-256 `adc1372287074d281269d665c8a87bc529aaf6769b0a2b6afcf02b8a24fd3e5e`; executed canonical rule hash `b51165a71f58`.

The authority translates each largest same-color component so its **bounding-box top-left** lands on the singleton marker. Every one of the generator’s five static shapes contains local cell `(0,0)`. Across 1,000 samples in each of easy, medium, and hard—6,000 generated colored shapes total—the bounding-box top-left was occupied every time. Therefore the shortcut “translate the lexicographically first occupied shape cell to the marker” is indistinguishable on the generated distribution.

`checks/audit/60a64cbfe154/counterexample.json` supplies a 10×10 documented-domain witness with two colors, one singleton and one connected multi-cell shape per color, and in-bounds translations. The target’s own `self_check` returns no errors. One shape has an empty bounding-box top-left, so the supported canonical Racket output and the first-occupied-cell rival differ at four cells. The source-bound Racket receipt is `checks/audit/60a64cbfe154/racket.json`; the 6,000-shape scan is `checks/audit/60a64cbfe154/domain_scan.json`.

This is a generator-coverage defect/possible model shortcut, not a claim that the canonical rule is wrong. No audit target file was modified.
